chapter_theme: Serving a king is like warming oneself at a fire: useful, dangerous, and demanding constant awareness of distance. The chapter gives rules for courtiers who can't presume on favour, age, kinship or old intimacy, and is candid about the danger behind the courtesy.
structure_note: Parimelazhagar divides the chapter: general rules (691-693), specific conduct (694-697), and the warning that one shouldn't do what displeases on the assumption that he will bear with it (698-700).

691.reading: Those who attach themselves to quarrelsome kings should be like people warming at a fire: not going off, not going close.
691.nuance: The image avoids praising or blaming the king: fire doesn't have intentions. Parimelazhagar spells out both halves: at a distance one gets nothing, and up close one is burned. இகல் doesn't say which kings, and may imply all of them.

692.reading: Not desiring what kings desire brings, through those kings, lasting prosperity.
692.nuance: A kind of worldly detachment that works as strategy. Parimelazhagar gives the mechanism: kings fear those who would rival them in pleasures, finery and rank, and they reward one who doesn't. So the restraint is prudence and may not be virtue at all.

693.reading: If you would guard yourself, guard against the gravest things; once suspicion has arisen, nobody can clear it.
693.nuance: Parimelazhagar's list of grave faults is betrayal, intimacy with royal women and seizing treasure. His comparison is memorable: like a debt that comes to mind at each sight of the debtor, a cleared suspicion recurs each time the king sees you.

694.reading: In the presence of the great and established, suppress whispers and shared smiles.
694.nuance: These small signs are dangerous because a ruler reads them: Parimelazhagar says he will assume they concern his own faults. The next chapter's interest in reading signs here falls on those who are read. The verse says 'great ones', and only commentators limit this to kings.

695.reading: Don't listen in to anything or press for anything; hear a secret when it has been let go.
695.nuance: Manakkudavar says that even the desire to hear is a fault. The whole risk is that curiosity about power looks like a threat to it.

696.reading: Knowing the mood and considering the time, say what is needed and not disliked, so that it is wanted.
696.nuance: Each word is doing work: வெறுப்பில, 'not disliked', is a test of the hearer, while வேண்டுப, 'needed', is a test of the matter. Parimelazhagar explains that a thing a king doesn't accept won't get done, so the point is practical, and that during lust or anger advice is useless.

697.reading: Say what is wanted, and never say what is useless even if you are asked.

positions.position: Say what is of great benefit and desired, even if not asked, and don't say what is profitless, even if the king asks.
positions.quote: எஞ்ஞான்றும் பயனிலவாயவற்றைத் தானே கேட்டாலும் சொல்லாது விடுக.

positions.position: Say what the king wants; and if an enemy king questions an envoy about the size of the army, evade: 'Don't you know?'
positions.quote: பகையரசன் வினாவினால், நீ அறியாததொன்றோ வென்று அளவு கூறாமை.

698.reading: Without belittling him as 'he's younger' or 'he's kin of such a degree', one should conduct oneself in keeping with the light he stands in.
698.nuance: நின்ற ஒளி: the light is one he stands in, and this can be read as belonging to the office, whoever holds it. Pope's '(Divine)' comes from Parimelazhagar.

positions.position: The light is the king's divinity: he guards the world while asleep, and they must act as men before gods.
The light is simply the headship he has obtained.
positions.quote: அவர் பெற்று நின்ற தலைமையோடே பொருந்த ஒழுக வேண்டும்

positions.position: It is the eminence of those in positions of government.

699.reading: Those of unshaken clarity won't, thinking 'we are in favour', do what is unacceptable.
699.nuance: Parimelazhagar's diagnosis is one of changed self-image: those who fall think of themselves as new people after being favoured. Clarity, then, is seeing that one is the same person as before.

700.reading: The intimacy that, thinking 'we go back a long way', does what is improper brings ruin.
700.nuance: Parimelazhagar's explanation is the chapter's coldest note: when the king can no longer bear it, he takes the life without any kindly regard for the old bond. The chapter on kindly regard asks for exactly what the courtier here can't count on.

links.note: Both use கெழுதகைமை, the privilege of old intimacy. 803 asks what good long friendship is unless such liberties are accepted as if your own. 700 says to take such liberties with a king brings ruin. Friendship and power apply opposite rules to the same bond.

638 obliges the man at the king's side to tell him what is good, even if the king destroys wise counsel. 696 and 697 advise saying what is not disliked, in the way that he wants. The same courtier is told to be fearless and to be careful. Parimelazhagar narrows the gap by reading 'wanted' as also greatly beneficial.

582 makes it a king's work to know everything happening to everyone, swiftly and always. 695 tells those near him not even to listen in on his secrets. Knowledge flows one way, and the Kural presents this imbalance as prudence, not as a problem.

388 says a king who rules justly and protects is held to be a god among people: the title is earned. On Parimelazhagar's reading of 698, the divinity belongs to any king, young or kin, and the courtier mustn't ask. Other readings of ஒளி remove the conflict.

Chapter 57 tells the king not to be dreaded, and this chapter tells the courtier how to live with one who is. Both are realistic, and the Kural addresses each party without assuming the other has listened.

Almost the same phrase, துளக்கற்ற காட்சி and நடுக்கற்ற காட்சி. In 654 unshaken clarity won't do what is degrading, even in trouble. In 699 it won't presume on favour. Steadiness shows in both failure and success.

source_issues: 692: Pope's couplet and gloss are run together with a stray '< br>' tag, leaving the gloss field empty after the separator.
699: Parimelazhagar's explanation has a word missing its opening letter (ன்னையராகவே, likely தன்னையராகவே).
